items.title: Flames hoping to re-sign pending UFA Morgan Frost
items.summary: What could the center snag on his new deal?
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images This was always supposed to be another rebuilding year for the Calgary Flames . Despite a quietly decent start, nobody is expecting a major playoff push for the Flames. There have been several individual bright spots (winger Joel Farabee at the forefront) for the Flames this season. Though he may not be leading the charge offensively, center Morgan Frost has quietly become a consistent piece for the Flames up front since arriving two seasons ago from the Philadelphia Flyers. With five goals and 14 points through 23 games so far, Frost is on pace to surpass his previous career best of 46 points thanks to an 84-game pace of 51. Frost, 27, is in the final year of a two-year, $8.75 million contract he signed with the Flames two summers ago. Speaking with several team sources going back to the summer, the hope is for the Flames to re-sign Frost and keep him as part of the future beyond this season. Frost’s agent, Darren Ferris, is notorious for walking his players to free agency and playing hardball. At the age of 28 by the time his next contract kicks in, Frost could (theoretically) get one more “big’’ contract in his early thirties if he were to re-sign with the Flames on a mid-term deal. Speculatively speaking, a term in the four-year range could be the perfect ballpark for both the team and player. According to a league source, Montreal Canadiens forward Alex Newhook’s contract could be a good comparable as a starting point for Frost. The 25-year-old signed a four-year, $22.2 million extension with the Canadiens that is set to kick in next season. The comparison isn’t perfect, as one source pointed out. items.body: New Year’s Eve game to be played outdoors in shadow of Wasatch Mountains SALT LAKE CITY -- We stood on the 50-yard line in the middle of Rice-Eccles Stadium, the home of University of Utah football. It was empty, silent, a little cold. Traces of snow dotted the artificial turf. We could only imagine what it would be like for the Discover NHL Winter Classic on New Year’s Eve (6 p.m. ET; HBO MAX, truTV, TNT, SN, TVAS), when the Utah Mammoth will host the Colorado Avalanche outdoors and the field will look like a ski resort. “It literally gives you chills to think about how exciting it’s going to be,” said Brooke Croshier-Sidebotham, the vice president of stadium and arena operations at the University of Utah, as she gave NHL.com a tour Thursday. “This is a once-in-a-lifetime event that’s happening here in the stadium, and I think the excitement is unmatched.” The more you explore Rice-Eccles Stadium, the more excited you become. The stadium sits at the base of the Wasatch Mountains. The higher you sit facing east, the better the view. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Matt Zambonin/HHOF-IIHF Images One of the finest scorers in women’s hockey has finally put pen to paper. On Friday, the Montreal Victoire announced that the team has signed forward Petra Nieminen to a two-year contract, which will carry through the 2027-28 season. The Victoire took Nieminen in the first round, 12th overall, of the 2026 PWHL Draft . It was the first year that the Finnish star declared her intention to join the league. Nieminen comes to the league after establishing herself as one of the premier European players in the women’s game. The Tampere native led the SDHL in goals in three of the past four seasons, leading a strong Lulea HF squad by being the league’s leading scorer in back-to-back years. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Vilmer Salen Forsberg (Brandon Taylor OHL Images) Everyone knows goalies are the hardest to project. There’s one, Vilmer Salén Forsberg, who will probably appear at the top of every single list. Beyond that, though, you’re going to find plenty of variation. Some scouts are willing to take chances on smaller goalies with elite athleticism, while others will strictly target netminders with big frames. Personally, I always have a soft spot for guys who play well on bad teams. You have to look beyond the stats to see a goalie’s future, which is something the New Jersey Devils did when they drafted Mikhail Yegorov in the second round in 2024. Standard fantasy categories include goals, assists, power-play points, shots on goal, hits and blocked shots for skaters and wins, goals-against average, save percentage and shutouts for goalies. Value has been quantified based on factors including but not limited to past production in the regular season and Stanley Cup Playoffs, line combinations, defense pairs, power-play usage, team goalie situations, anticipated start volume, projected goal support (or lack thereof), injury history or concern, age, contract status and overall upside for the 2026-27 season. items.summary: The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to build a two-game win streak were wholly absent in Seattle.
items.body: SEATTLE — Winning streaks. So hard to build, so easy to blow. After waiting 23 games to construct their first two-game winning streak of the National Hockey League season, the Vancouver Canucks never gave themselves a chance here Thursday to count to three. Actually, goalie Leevi Merilainen gave the Canucks a chance, but he was about the only one. Teammates didn’t respond or rally around his brilliant performance through 28 minutes and eventually lost 5-1 to the Seattle Kraken. The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to respond to difficult stretches or untimely goals-against in their surprising wins this week against the Vegas Golden Knights and Utah Mammoth were wholly absent in Seattle. After getting outshot 24-5 in the opening period, the Canucks surrendered another nine shots in the first nine minutes of the second. The Kraken scored twice in 54 seconds, starting at the eight-minute mark, to pull ahead 3-1. And given the avalanche of shots and Kraken skaters bombarding Merilainen’s net, the Canucks never looked capable of coming back from two goals down. The Canucks have false-started in a pile of games this season, and posted absolute duds in a few. But even for a last-place team, their reversal in form from Las Vegas and Salt Lake City was surprising. “A little bit,” Canucks coach Manny Malhotra conceded. “Just in terms of how off we were and how badly we got outshot. (I was) expecting a better response. I think the guys had a much clearer understanding coming into tonight that we earned what we got in our previous two games just by the work ethic — the winning of puck battles, establishing a forecheck, those types of things. The Golden Knights were on the power play down 2-0 at this point of the game, and after Jack Eichel passed the puck to Stone behind the net, the Vegas captain made a quick pass across the slot to Victor Olofsson, who did what he does best and buried it with a one-timer. With the assist, Stone gets the 418th point of his Golden Knights career, and puts him atop the franchise’s all-time scoring records. Stone isn’t entirely safe as the team’s all-time scoring leader though, as center William Karlsson is only five points behind the Golden Knights captain. Ovechkin’s 763rd assist to surpass Nicklas Backstrom ’s Capitals record was mostly a footnote following a 6-3 loss to the Buffalo Sabres at Capital One Arena on Thursday. It was the fourth consecutive loss for Washington, which allowed at least five goals in each of the defeats, and fell to a disappointing 10-10-0 through its first 20 games. “We just have to keep fighting,” Ovechkin said. “Sometimes things don't go your way, but we just have to keep fighting and stay with it.” Ovechkin has been fighting it all season. The NHL’s all-time leader with 930 goals has scored just one through his first 20 games and was held without one for the 15th straight game Thursday. That’s the longest goal drought of his 22-season NHL career, exceeding one of 14 games from Nov. 22-Dec. 20, 2023. The 41-year-old left wing has six points (one goal, five assists) this season, including just two (both assists) in his past 12 games. “Chances are there,” Ovechkin said. “It’s just sometimes you hold the stick too tight. Just stick with it and keep working.” After Ovechkin announced on Oct. 5 that this will be his final season in the NHL, the Capitals hoped to send him off with another run at the Stanley Cup. The 22-year-old left winger was the first NHL player with a goal in 10 consecutive games since Teemu Selanne set the Anaheim record with an 11-game run in 1997. Gauthier had four hat tricks during the streak, including Tuesday night in an 8-6 defeat at St. Louis. items.title: Maple Leafs gain point, but fall to Kings to extend winless streak
items.summary: For now, the Maple Leafs will have to settle for a single point gained, a small step forward even if it comes amid continued stumbles.
items.body: TORONTO — For a moment Thursday night, it seemed the Toronto Maple Leafs had found some progress. Some momentum, some life. For the first time in this stretch of what's now eight straight games without a win, the Maple Leafs made their way to the locker room after 20 minutes with a two-goal lead and their opponents held off the board. A much-needed power-play marker from Auston Matthews had drawn first blood against the visiting Los Angeles Kings. The captain then set up another, dancing through the offensive zone and finding John Tavares. Fourth-liners Brandon Duhaime and Teddy Blueger dropped the gloves with a couple of Kings before the period was through, sending Toronto to the room with a pair of goals and a pair of fights. Two minutes into the second period, the home side kept it rolling. items.title: Lane Hutson leads Canadiens to gutsiest win of season
items.summary: The Hurricanes tried to push them. But Lane Hutson and the Canadiens didn’t just get up and push back, they pushed the Hurricanes over in a way they haven’t been able to in recent memory.
items.body: This was Lane Hutson as we’ve never seen him before — doubled over, gasping for the air that had been knocked out of him by the type of hit he’s so rarely been on the receiving end of since he jitterbugged his way into the NHL at the end of the 2023-24 season. Hutson was uncharacteristically lackadaisical, atypically unaware of Shayne Gostisbehere’s presence. He never saw it coming. But it was Gostisbehere and the Carolina Hurricanes who, in the end, were on the end of an unforeseen outcome. Because Hutson bounced back up from that second-period hit that left him winded and eventually took everyone’s breath away. First with a stunner of a tying goal late in the third period. And then with the winner that made it 2-1 Montreal Canadiens in overtime to cap their gutsiest performance of the season. “Everyone stepped up,” Hutson told reporters at Lenovo Center. That was right after Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis referred to it as a win that made them “better as a team.” It’s exactly what we were thinking with each passing minute of the game, as the Canadiens finally bore their teeth against this hungry pack of wolves. Oh sure, they beat the Hurricanes three times last regular season and once more at the start of the Eastern Conference Final last spring. But none of those games looked like this one, with the Canadiens pinching all the pressure points the Hurricanes typically have a firm grasp of. That they did it less than 24 hours after registering a bounce-back win against the red-hot Devils in New Jersey, that they did it missing several key players, and that they did it against a Hurricanes team that’s still sitting with the NHL’s best points percentage (.795) despite the loss, said everything about how much their character has grown since that lopsided playoff series.

items.body: The Minnesota Wild picked up a 4-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Thursday, but it may have come at a price. Superstar defenceman Quinn Hughes exited late in the contest after he was on the receiving end of a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka midway through the third period. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Alex Ovechkin broke Nicklas Backstrom’s Washington Capitals franchise record for most career assists with a primary helper on Boone Jenner’s goal in the third period of Thursday’s game against the Buffalo Sabres . Ovechkin, 41, picked up his fifth assist of the 2026-27 season — and the 763rd of his NHL career — at the 9:44 mark of the third period at Capital One Arena. The long-serving Capitals captain didn’t have much to do with the goal itself , sending a casual pass to Jenner in the neutral zone … before chaos ensued. Jenner sent a backhand dump-in attempt directly towards Sabres goaltender Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, who bobbled the puck before losing track of it entirely, allowing Jenner to tap it between his pads and into the net. Ovechkin was already on the Capitals’ bench by the time Jenner scored, and as such, he didn’t receive credit for a plus on the play. To open up the spot star defenseman Cale Makar has landed on injured reserve, reported by Ryan O’Hara of The Hockey News . Beckman, 25, will have the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since April 2024 as a member of the Wild. Drafted by Minnesota in the third round seven years ago, the winger broke the 100-point mark in his last full junior season as a Spokane Chief, generating some hype with his high end shot and making a quick Wild debut at age 20. Suiting up for 22 more games over the years with three assists, at this point he has made most of his impact in the AHL. Proving himself as a reliable scorer for the Iowa Wild with defensive shortcomings, not uncommon for non-prospects who light up the AHL, the Saskatoon native Beckman made stops with the Utica Comets and Bridgeport Islanders. He put together a 30-goal campaign last season for the New York farm club prior to catching on as part of the Avalanche organization. Usually they take about two weeks,” Falkenberg said. “Pepsi supplied the boxes and they all come in flat, so I have to fold them all into shape and then assemble them into pieces and transport them down.” Falkenberg has worked for Save-On-Foods in Kelowna, B.C., for the past 28 years and has been building displays for stores in the province for the past 10 years. items.summary: New NHL coaches are often the opposite of the bench bosses they've replaced, but has Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller really been different, or in any way better, than Craig Berube?
items.body: David Banks-Imagn Images David Banks-Imagn Images Opinion: Wasn't Jim Hiller Supposed To Help The Toronto Maple Leafs Become A Better Defensive Team? Adam Proteau Partner Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Published Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Updated Nov 20, 2026 12:45 AM New NHL coaches are often the opposite of the bench bosses they've replaced, but has Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller really been different, or in any way better, than Craig Berube? As is often the case when NHL teams change coaches, the organization's choice for a new coach is someone with a significantly different philosophy than that of their predecessor. A team that failed with a coach who was more rigid or autocratic in their approach almost always ends up replaces him with a more player-friendly bench boss — and vice versa. So, when the Toronto Maple Leafs fired coach Craig Berube at the end of last season and replaced him with Jim Hiller, the idea was that Hiller would succeed at turning Toronto into a better defensive team than the one Berube tried to mold to fit his approach. Both go about their business in different ways, but has Hiller actually succeeded where Berube couldn't? items.body: Register Login Avalanche’s Gabriel Landeskog, Parker Kelly Fined By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 5:00 pm The NHL’s Department of Player Safety has issued two separate fines from last night’s contest between the Colorado Avalanche and the Utah Mammoth. First, the DoPS fined Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog $5,000 (the maximum allowable) for cross-checking Mammoth forward Logan Cooley . The DoPS also fined Avalanche forward Parker Kelly $3,500 for high-sticking Mammoth forward Michael Carcone . There was an immediate expectation that Landeskog would face supplemental discipline. Early in the contest, Cooley attempted to hit Landeskog, and he ended up rolling over his back. Cooley attempted to stand up, but Landeskog repeatedly cross-checked him, even while he was on the ice, until he was eventually pulled off. The referees assessed Landeskog a double-minor for the incident. This isn’t the first time Landeskog has had a run-in with the Department of Player Safety. The former second-overall pick has been suspended four different times throughout his 13-year career, for 11 games total. Today’s discipline is his second career fine. The last time he was fined was during the 2014-15 season for punching the Minnesota Wild’s former captain, Mikko Koivu . Meanwhile, this is Kelly’s first time being fined. Still, like Landeskog, he’s faced discipline from the Department of Player Safety before. Toward the end of the 2023-24 campaign, Kelly received a two-game suspension for an illegal check to the head against Los Angeles Kings defenseman Andreas Englund . Landeskog would probably rather pay the fine than take the beating Jack McBain put on him last night. That was an a** wuppin!

items.summary: Filip Gustavsson went 28-15-6 with a .904 SV% and four shutouts in 50 games with the Minnesota Wild in 2025-26.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Minnesota Wild announced Thursday that goaltender Filip Gustavsson has been assigned to their AHL affiliate on a conditioning stint. He is expected to start for the Iowa Wild this Saturday against the San Diego Gulls. Gustavsson, 28, underwent hip surgery in the summer and started the season on injured reserve . In 2025-26, he went 28-15-6 with a .904 save percentage (SV%) and a 1.4 goals saved above expected (GSAx) with four shutouts in 50 games. This season will be the first in a five-year, $34-million contract extension that Gustavsson signed in October 2025. He will carry a cap hit of $6.8 million through the 2030-31 campaign. In six NHL seasons, the Skelleftea, Sweden, native is 111-74-26 with a .911 SV% and a 2.67 goals against average (GAA) in 219 appearances with the Wild and Ottawa Senators . He also has a 4-7 record with a .911 SV% and 2.67 GAA in 12 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. Gustavsson was taken in the second round of the 2016 NHL Entry Draft by the Pittsburgh Penguins . He spent two more seasons developing in Sweden’s top professional hockey league with Lulea HF before he moved to North America. In 2018, Gustavsson was traded to the Senators, along with Ian Cole, a first-round pick and a third-round pick in exchange for Derick Brassard. He spent parts of five seasons with their AHL affiliate, the Belleville Senators, where he posted a 45-39-8 record with an .898 SV% and 3.06 GAA in 95 appearances.

items.title: Report: Simon Edvinsson passed on multiple offer sheets to force exit from Red Wings
items.summary: Edvinsson must sign by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 to be eligible to play in the NHL this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The situation between the Detroit Red Wings and defenseman Simon Edvinsson keeps getting uglier. Edvinsson, 23, is currently a restricted free agent, having not yet signed an extension with the Red Wings following the completion of his three-year, entry-level deal last season. He must sign a deal by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 in order to be eligible to play in the NHL this season. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli, Edvinsson has turned down offer sheets from multiple teams in order to deny Detroit the opportunity to match, putting pressure on the Red Wings to simply trade him before the December 1 deadline. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” a source told Seravalli. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff mentioned earlier this season that he has “zero interest” in trading Edvinsson. Horcoff may be forced to change his tune, or else risk losing Edvinsson for the season if nothing gets done ahead of the December 1 deadline. Detroit would still retain Edvinsson’s rights in that case, but would presumably receive less appealing trade offers for a player that could no longer play this season. Seravalli also pointed out that there is a daily cap penalty for the first year of a contract given to a restricted free agent after the start of the regular season, meaning the cap hit for this season on any deal Edvinsson may ultimately sign gets higher with each day he remains unsigned. Selected sixth overall by the Red Wings in the 2021 NHL Entry Draft, Edvinsson had nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in 72 games with Detroit last season, while averaging just under 22 and half minutes of ice time.

The clock is ticking. Horcoff and the Red Wings seem comfortable making the Edvinsson camp sweat by taking it to the deadline, now just 12 days away. items.body: Utah defeats Colorado in chippy game that features big hits, multiple fights SALT LAKE CITY -- If the Utah Mammoth and Colorado Avalanche play outdoors New Year’s Eve the way they did indoors Wednesday, it won’t just be chilly. It’ll be chippy. Utah won 4-1 at Delta Center in an intense, physical game that Mammoth coach Andre Tourigny hopes is a preview of the Discover NHL Winter Classic . “That would be pretty good, eh?” Tourigny said with a smile. “Honestly, what you want more than that? Great fights. Great hits. The bodychecks were flying. The two teams did not like each other, were going at each other, played the right way, played hard. That’s a good night for hockey.” When Utah joined the NHL in 2024-25, one of the questions was which team would become its rival. Colorado seemed logical, if only because the two teams shared geography, topography and the Central Division. Colorado-Utah wasn’t much of a rivalry the past two seasons. The Avalanche went 5-1-1 against the Mammoth, including 3-0-1 at Delta Center. The teams had no history of animosity. items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Hours before the Montreal Canadiens bounced back from what Martin St. Louis termed to be “pretty much the worst” game they’d played this season, the coach sung his most common refrain. “All team sports are the same,” St. Louis began. “I didn’t invent these rules of being in space and breaking pressure with being in balance on the ice. When you play inside that, you raise your percentages of having success and you get the bounces. When you don’t do that, your percentages of having success go down and you go looking for bounces. When you do things the right way, you get goals and bounces and a high percentage of success.” That was what he said at his morning media availability. Then St. Louis shuffled one player on each of his four lines and two of his three defence pairings, and the Canadiens went out and proved to themselves that if they play the way they’re supposed to, it doesn’t matter who they're on the ice with. items.body: Ottawa Senators rookie Tyler Boucher will have a friendly face calling his game for the opposition broadcast on Thursday. His dad, former NHLer Brian Boucher, will be in the booth for NBC Philadelphia's local broadcast when the Philadelphia Flyers visit the Senators on Thursday — a game in which the younger Boucher is expected to play. "I mean, I'm going to try to keep it as normal as possible, treat him like another player, but I am going to be keeping a close eye on him for sure," Brian told NHL.com's Dan Rosen on Wednesday. "I've got to be honest with you, I've dreamt about this moment since he's been drafted. For me personally, I don't know about for him, but since I got into this side of the game I've always been like, 'Man, it would be so cool to call his games.' It would be really meaningful to me. I've never told him that because I've never wanted to put pressure on him, but for me personally it's going to be a special moment and I'm looking forward to it if it does happen." Brian played for the Flyers for six seasons in three separate stints before his retirement following the 2012-13 season. Tyler was selected by the Senators with the 10th-overall pick of the 2021 draft and made his debut on Tuesday night — scoring his first NHL goal in the process. The elder Boucher said that while he doesn't consider himself to be a typical hockey dad, he admitted that it's "better to be upstairs so (Tyler) doesn't see my facial reactions." items.title: Canadiens end power-play drought in win, hand Hellebuyck 1st Devils loss
items.body: NEWARK, N.J. — Jake Evans scored the go-ahead goal, captain Nick Suzuki ended his team's long power-play drought and the Montreal Canadiens defeated the New Jersey Devils 3-2 on Wednesday night to halt a two-game skid. Connor Hellebuyck got a piece of Evans' shot with his glove but could not keep it out of the net. The goal with 13:43 left sparked “Go, Habs, go!” chants from the many Canadiens fans in attendance. Hellebuyck allowed three goals on 27 shots and lost for the first time in eight starts since joining New Jersey in a trade from Winnipeg in late October. Despite Timo Meier setting up a goal by Luke Evangelista and scoring on a breakaway fresh out of the penalty box, the Devils had their two-game winning streak snapped, losing for just the second time in their past nine. The Canadiens only trailed for 40 seconds after Evangelista's goal, as Alex Newhook got in on net and made a nifty move to beat Hellebuyck and tie it. After spending time practicing the power play on Tuesday and devoting significant conversation to what was going wrong, they came up empty on their first two chances. With Montreal's run at 0 for its past 14, a parade to the penalty box eventually came back to bite New Jersey. Suzuki drew a tripping penalty on Brenden Dillon, then deflected Lane Hutson's point shot in past Hellebuyck with 41.9 seconds remaining in the first period. Jacob Fowler stopped all 20 shots he faced in the second and third, finishing with 27 saves and avoiding what would have been his first time losing consecutive games this season. He and his teammates successfully killed a penalty in the final minutes to seal it.
